A continuing tenant may receive no more than two increases in any 12-month period, and increase notices must follow Civ. Code § 827.",

Mobilehome tenancies are covered for increases on or after 2021-02-18, and other housing for increases on or after 2019-03-15. The cap does not apply to a homeowner of a mobilehome. The owner may set the initial rent for a new tenancy in which no prior tenant remains in lawful possession. Waivers are void.",
      "exemptions": "(1) Deed-restricted or regulatory-restricted affordable housing for very low, low or moderate income households, or housing subject to an affordable-housing subsidy agreement. (2) Dormitories owned and operated by a higher-education institution or a K-12 school. (3) Housing subject to a valid local rent or price control that limits annual increases to less than the state cap. (4) Housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, applied on a rolling basis (not applicable to mobilehomes). (5) A two-unit property where the owner occupied the second unit for the entire tenancy. (6) Residential property alienable separate from title to any other dwelling unit, such as single-family homes and condominiums. This exemption applies only if the property is not owned by a real estate trust, a corporation, or an LLC with at least one corporate member, and only if the landlord gave the tenant the required written notice.
